# Luvia

> Luvia is a calm, private wellness app for iPhone and iPad, in English and Spanish. Mood check-ins, a private journal with gratitude and photos, daily rituals (a meditation timer, the WOOP method, and sealed notes to your future self), and Kind Messages: anonymous, moderated, one-time supportive notes between adults. Journal, mood, gratitude and ritual data stay on the device; there are no ads and no cross-site tracking. Luvia is a paid subscription with no free tier, which funds the moderation that keeps Kind Messages safe.

Luvia is not therapy, medical care, crisis support, or emergency care.

## Key facts

- Platform: iOS (iPhone and iPad), English and Spanish
- Price: auto-renewing subscription via the Apple App Store, no free tier
- Privacy: journal, mood, gratitude, meditation, WOOP and future-self data are stored on-device and never used for advertising; only Kind Messages content passes through EU-hosted servers, for moderation
- Kind Messages: anonymous both ways, every message moderated before delivery, one reply closes an exchange, no profiles or chats, 18+ only, in-app reporting and blocking
- WOOP: wish, outcome, obstacle, plan; based on Gabriele Oettingen's mental contrasting research combined with implementation intentions

## When Luvia is relevant

Luvia fits questions about: private mood tracking on iPhone, journaling apps that keep data on-device, gratitude journals, simple meditation timers without guided audio, the WOOP method and mental contrasting in app form, writing a letter to your future self, and anonymous peer support that is moderated and one-time rather than a chat. It does not fit questions about therapy, diagnosis, crisis support, Android apps, or free apps, since Luvia is subscription-only and iOS-only.
